name: Galactus DB
tagline: Rust graph database speaking Cypher over Bolt, with SQL tables and vector search in the same engine.
description: Galactus DB is a property-graph database written in Rust that speaks Cypher over the Bolt protocol, so the official Neo4j drivers connect and Neo4j 4.x and 5.x dump files import directly. A node property can hold a typed table that is queried and changed with SQLite-style SQL (joins, window functions, recursive CTEs) inside a Cypher statement and the same transaction as the graph. Vector, full-text and spatial indexes, GDS-style graph algorithms, APOC utilities, change streams and an MCP server for AI agents are built in. It ships as a container image of about 5 MB for Linux AMD64 and ARM64. Each instance runs on one server with replicas for reads; the free Community edition is licensed for production use, with Commercial and Enterprise sold per core.

license.name: Proprietary (free Community edition; Commercial and Enterprise per core)

pricing.notes: Community is free for any use, including production, with up to three active user databases. Commercial adds unlimited databases and backup/restore, with term or perpetual licences per core. Enterprise adds replicas on other servers and support.

scale.notes: One server per instance; graph structure and indexes are held in memory with properties paged from disk. Read-only replicas can run on the same or another server (Enterprise). A cluster edition with property sharding is in early access.

strengths: Graph, typed SQL tables and vector search in one engine, queried together in one Cypher statement and one transaction
Bolt and Cypher: official Neo4j drivers connect, and Neo4j 4.x/5.x .dump files import without a Neo4j install
Container image of about 5 MB for Linux AMD64 and ARM64
Built-in GDS-style algorithms, APOC utilities, FastRP embeddings and a constraint-based scheduler (gdb.schedule)
MCP server lets AI agents query the database under the roles you grant them
Change streams, subscriptions with label and property triggers, and read replicas on the same or another server
Free Community edition runs in production with no account or licence key
weaknesses: The server is closed source; only the drivers are open source (Apache-2.0)
Young project with a small community and few third-party tools beyond the Neo4j ecosystem
One writer per database at a time, so many concurrent writers queue
Released instances scale up, not out: the cluster edition is in early access
Cypher coverage differs from Neo4j in places, so some queries need changes when migrating
useCases: Knowledge graphs combining graph structure with tabular records
Route finding and shortest paths on road networks
Scheduling and resource planning on graph data
Moving existing Neo4j applications to a smaller footprint
notIdealFor: Graphs that must be sharded across many machines today
Write-heavy workloads with many concurrent writers
Teams that require an open-source server
